questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As an English student, I wanted to go to an English-speaking country that was within Europe. So it was quite given that the UK would be an obvious choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. They did zoom-meeting where you got a lot of necessary information as well as online modules to go through. It could be information-heavy but it was very nice and handy. They also provided a document with all necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Manchester provided a lot of information, and they were very easy to get in contact with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My boyfriend and I shared an AIRBNB during our entire stay. This was what fulfilled our personal needs and we really enjoyed staying there. We lived in the Chorlton/Whalley Range area which was super nice and felt safe. However, it is expensive, so I wouldn't recommend it unless you are two people sharing the expenses.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The Bee Network works phenomenally. If you live off-campus, consider buying a buss term pass – it is almost like a Danish "ungdomskort", but only works for busses. However, you can then travel as much as you like in an extended period.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I talked to a lot of people living in student housing. A lot were complaining about the facilities or flat mates' hygiene. I think for one semester it is durable and you take it for what it is. Just don't expect luxury.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Their registration website was quite easy to navigate. However, some choices or questions didn't seem applicable to Danish exchange students, but the university provided a lot of help and guidance.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You access a website which takes you through the process. It saves your answers and lets you know if you haven't answered something particular. It was very easy to use.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university answers very quickly on email. So don't worry about waiting a long time for an answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to register twice for classes. I registered about twelve classes in total and got four of them. I had to drop a course due to timetable clashes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possible. In terms of classes, I would recommend applying for as many as you can/or find interesting. You might not get your first priorities so you need to be flexible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two first year courses and one second year. I enjoyed the second year the most because other students tended to take the class more seriously and the professor expected more. The first year courses were really interesting but tended to not challenge me enough.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: If you do humanities you can expect some assignments to allow for more creativity than the usual UCPH style of assignments. For one class, I did a hashtag analysis and designed my own social media campaign as part of my assessment.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
DIGI10062: Digital Activism
DIGI24232: Digital Ways of Seeing: Theory and Practice
PHIL10622: Introduction to Metaphysics and Epistemology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend DIGI24232: Digital Ways of Seeing: Theory and Practice. I learned a lot from it and it was also quite practical (obviously). In one of the last classes, we tried the university's VR-headsets. It was a lot of fun and I really enjoyed this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not really experience any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Trains are quite expensive in the UK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The SU (student's union) at UOM is amazing. There are so many activities and societies to participate in. They also had a thing called "sporticipate" where you can try out different sports during the week at beginner level. It costs you 1 pound to try out any classes for the entire semester. You just sign up for the events through the SU's own website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'd recommend the International Society day trips. I went to the Brönte museum in Haworth and Holyhead in Wales. Both were amazing trips and you meet other international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can easily spend a day walking around Manchester and see the different museums – and most of them have free access.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The English culture is not too far from the Danish. Perhaps expect people to approach you more.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend student societies. Also go to pubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: First years are a lot of teenagers who moved out for the first time, and you can tell. In some instances, you are going to feel quite old compared to them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pubculture is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. UOM has amazing study facilities. Al G is the best!
2. Go to the uni and figure out where your classrooms are before your classes start.
3. You are always going to feel like you don't do enough, but you are. Embrace your need to relax and enjoy it when you are out and doing stuff. You don't need to do more or less.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Office hours are a big deal at UOM. Professors seem more approachable because they invite you to come talk to them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding thing was the fact that I wen't to a place I knew nothing about, but now know like the back of my hand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not seeing my family and friends back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The UOM is extremely accessible. If you have any type of disability, they will attempt to accommodate you. Even the buildings are accessible in many different ways.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
